term: expected utility, rational action, belief, and truth
resolution: value compares extended nonnegative expected utilities in an explicitly stipulated two-state reward profile. A mixed act independently selects the rewarded act with weight q. It does not select whether a proposition is true and does not model an ability to choose belief. Equality at top defeats strict ranking by this value alone; it does not prove indifference under every decision rule, a duty to randomize, or that any religious hypothesis is true. Positive weights, bounded-probability interpretation, payoff assignments and any maximizing norm remain open application commitments. No signed-cost claim is made.
